structured_output.assessment:
The three chapters are technically careful, and the scientific qualifications are strong. The main prose problem is rhythm: many paragraphs are runs of short declarative sentences, each restating one rule or one limit, so the logical links (because, whereas, so, although) are left for the reader to supply. These replacements join those runs into connected argument and keep short sentences where they act as deliberate boundary statements (for example, "Gross movement is a total, not a rate."). They also fix two grammar errors: "Both memory types are cleared ... and is copied" in Chapter 3 and "will report ... and do not label" in Chapter 3's telemetry section.

All numbers, thresholds, citation keys, \ref/\label/\href commands, equations, instrument anchors and the example utterance ``go back down'' are kept verbatim. The implemented-versus-proposed distinctions are unchanged, as are the pending-results framing and the separation between gaze confirmation, controller confirmation and trigger completion. Chapter 4 keeps its existing no-Oxford-comma style.

There are no main.tex edits because the abstract wasn't among the supplied files. I left captions, tables, figure fallback text, instrument descriptions and already-cohesive paragraphs unchanged on purpose.

edits.old: To give guidance continuity, the system maintains two short-term memories. A spatial history tracks turning progress and supports cues that return the participant to the target. A speech-decision memory records what the system actually said and how the guidance state changed. Each speech entry stores its relative age, context, and whether playback completed or was interrupted; each state entry stores the prior and current states and the reason for the transition. The speech and transition lists each retain at most four entries; snapshots sent to Jev exclude entries older than 15 seconds. This bounded recent context is related to the context-management motivation of EmBARDiment~\cite{bovo2025embardiment}, but the current implementation does not use its object-admission or dropout policy. The separate spatial history retains up to three seconds or 384 target-relative gaze observations and clears on invalid evidence, source changes, or observation gaps longer than 100~ms. These limits are engineering settings, not validated fixation or blink thresholds. Gaze-vicinity confirmation currently requires 100~ms of valid qualifying evidence; invalid evidence resets its entry timer, and reacquisition after a spoken confirmation requires 150~ms of valid gaze away. Those interaction gates do not admit objects to speech memory, and missing gaze is not counted as observed dwell. Both memory types are cleared whenever guidance resets and is copied before each asynchronous request. This memory is deliberately scoped to the current task: it does not build a persistent participant profile or attempt to infer unobserved mental states.

edits.old: Jev selects from a constrained set of options rather than generating free-form instructions. Local geometry and state rules first filter the phrase library to candidates that are valid in the current situation. Each request to Jev contains a state snapshot, recent memory, playback status, and two to five eligible phrases. Jev then chooses the wording and whether to speak now or wait. Target definition and geometric reasoning remain local. Eligibility filtering and playback revalidation are intended to reduce spatially incorrect or stale guidance, but tracking error, imperfect geometry and software faults can still produce unhelpful instructions; recorded-sequence and headset checks remain necessary.
